reference: The ts contracts are handwritten from docs/opus-ts.md, the Tree-sitter JSON grammar and byte-position rules, and the fixed expectations in tests/opus-ts-highlight.py (which docs/opus-ts.md identifies as handwritten); UTF-8 byte positions are counted from the literal input. No expected output was read from the pinned review candidate. A broader differential is deferred because the runner has no matching upstream tree-sitter CLI/grammar reference.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata for the ts loadable
JSON parse root shape and query byte offsets/columns with a multibyte character before a capture
JSON highlight winning spans and ANSI rendering for an object key and number
Tree handle child-path lookup, node type/range/text, and invalidation after free
Incremental edit generation invalidation and correct highlighted spans
Rejected edit range preserves the old source; unknown-language status
exclusions: No testing or changes to hl, nano, or other loadables.
No full upstream Tree-sitter differential across all bundled grammars or arbitrary query syntax; see the deferred case.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash metadata contract: ts is a builtin and Bash can retrieve its short help synopsis.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t ts) == builtin ]]; help -s ts > metadata.out; printf 'builtin\nhelp available\n'

cases.purpose: Parse the valid JSON scalar null and check the documented root S-expression shape. The invisible JSON value supertype is omitted from Tree-sitter's printed tree.
Check that query positions and byte ranges count UTF-8 bytes: the two-byte é precedes the number capture on the same line.
Check the documented non-overlapping winner for a JSON key, the number span, and SGR rendering transitions for the fixed source bytes.
cases.script: printf '%s' '{"k":1}' | ts highlight -L json -S; printf '%s' '{"k":1}' | ts highlight -L json

cases.purpose: Resolve a node through absolute child indices including anonymous punctuation, then verify its documented byte range and exact source text; freeing the tree invalidates its handle. Preserve failure diagnostics in harness stderr.
cases.script:
ts parse-tree -L json -t T < <(printf '%s' '{"a":[1]}')
ts node-type "$T:0,1,2,1"
ts node-range "$T:0,1,2,1"
ts node-text "$T:0,1,2,1"
printf '\n'
ts free "$T"
if ts node-type "$T"; then printf 'stale=0\n'; else rc=$?; printf 'stale=%s\n' "$rc"; fi

cases.purpose: Replace the whole five-byte JSON array with a seven-byte object, check that the old generation stops resolving, and check the documented key/number spans on the edited tree. Preserve failure diagnostics in harness stderr.
cases.script:
ts parse-tree -L json -t T < <(printf '%s' '["k"]')
old=$T
ts edit "$T" 0 5 7 -t T < <(printf '%s' '{"k":1}')
if ts node-type "$old"; then printf 'stale=0\n'; else rc=$?; printf 'stale=%s\n' "$rc"; fi
ts highlight -t "$T" -S
ts free "$T"

cases.purpose: Supply a range whose prefix/suffix do not describe the actual source change; the documented rejection must leave the original tree source usable. Preserve failure diagnostics in harness stderr.
cases.script:
ts parse-tree -L json -t T < <(printf '%s' '{"a":1}')
if ts edit "$T" 1 2 2 -t T < <(printf '%s' '{"b":1}'); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'edit status=%s\n' "$rc"
ts node-text "$T"
printf '\n'
ts free "$T"

cases.purpose: Check the documented usage status for an unknown grammar name without depending on diagnostic wording. Preserve failure diagnostics in harness stderr.
cases.script:
: > empty
if ts parse -L absent < empty; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: A full parser/query differential across all five bundled grammars would validate broad compatibility beyond the small documented contracts.
cases.reason: This needs a reference tool that is absent from the image: a tree-sitter CLI built at the bundled grammar revisions. That is an image addition owned by root, not a new execution capability.

cases.purpose: Create, copy, link, rename and remove ordinary relative fixtures, then query the surviving JSON file through ts. The reference adapter uses jq to select the numeric value and independently counted byte coordinates for this fixed document. Compare output plus full file modes, bytes, hardlinks and symlink targets.
cases.script:
mkdir -p fixture/sub
touch fixture/sub/input
printf '%s\n' '{"k":[1,true]}' > fixture/sub/input
cp fixture/sub/input fixture/copy
ln fixture/copy fixture/hard
ln -s final fixture/sym
chmod 640 fixture/copy
mv fixture/copy fixture/final
ln fixture/final fixture/remove-me
unlink fixture/remove-me
rm fixture/sub/input
rmdir fixture/sub
printf 'fixture file operations completed\n'
if [[ $(type -t ts) == builtin ]]; then
 ts query -L json -q '(number) @n' < fixture/final
else
 value=$(jq -r '.k[0]' fixture/final)
 [[ $value == 1 ]]
 printf 'n 1:7-1:8 6-7 %s\n' "$value"
fi
